title: How noise-cancelling headphones work
length_scale_note: 1.32 keeps this script inside 150-170 wpm (1.38 gave 150.8 wpm).
pronunciation_notes: 'noise-cancelling' (hyphen) is spoken as 'noise-gancelling'; written 'noise cancelling' is clear. 'Where the noise pushes the air' was heard as 'Whether noise'; replaced by 'When the noise squeezes the air'.

segments.text: How do noise cancelling headphones work?
They don't just block noise. They add sound, to make silence.
Step one: a tiny microphone on the outside listens to the noise around you.
Step two: a chip flips the sound wave upside down, and the speaker plays it into your ear. It's called anti-noise.
When the noise squeezes the air, the anti-noise wave stretches it. The two waves cancel each other out.
Step three, the catch: this works best on steady, low sounds, like the hum of an engine or an air conditioner.
Sudden sounds, like a barking dog, and voices are harder to copy, so some of them still get through.
So your headphones don't just block noise. They play its exact opposite.

https://www.bose.com/stories/how-do-noise-cancelling-headphones-work (Bose: 'voices are harder to cancel than steady background noise because they change quickly and cover a wider range of sound.
